title: Six Kepler quarters support light contamination of KOI-3006.01 that changes with detector season
abstract: We tested nearby Kepler signals for matching periods and transit times. A strict timing screen found 707 pairs in a selected sample of 7,679 DR25 objects. Four pairs had no ephemeris contamination flag on either member. The two DR25 candidates in these four pairs are already false positives in the retrieved cumulative catalog. We checked KOI-3006.01 and its nearby deep eclipsing source in six Kepler quarters. The shallow target depth changes with detector season, while the source eclipse persists. SAP and PDC flux give similar results. This supports light contamination and the existing false-positive classification. It does not establish a new planet. The package includes a timing audit, phase controls, all used light curves, data hashes, code, and a reproduction script. No pixel data or independent telescope was used, so the light transfer path and the true binary host remain uncertain.

display.caption: Local eclipse depths in six Kepler quarters. Error bars give five-event block bootstrap standard errors. The shallow target changes with detector season. The nearby deep source persists.
Nearby ephemeris matches and the conditional phase control in the selected DR25 sample.
